bankLabel: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009) PBQ Arena Production Campaign

missions.title: Trace the Seven-Layer Signal
missions.briefing: A packet-analysis team must classify each observed function by its OSI layer.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Copper signaling and bit timing on an Ethernet link.
MAC addressing and frame delivery on a local segment.
IP forwarding between separate subnets.
Reliable application delivery using TCP acknowledgments.

explanations.task-1: Electrical signaling belongs to the Physical layer.
explanations.task-2: MAC frames operate at the Data Link layer.
explanations.task-3: IP routing is a Network-layer function.
explanations.task-4: TCP reliability operates at the Transport layer.

missions.title: Staff the Network Citadel
missions.objective: N10-009 1.2 — Networking appliances, applications, and functions
missions.briefing: Match each infrastructure requirement to the appliance that fulfills it most directly.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Forward traffic between IP networks.
Distribute client sessions across multiple application servers.
Inspect traffic and actively block recognized malicious patterns.
Provide centralized file storage over the existing LAN.
Relay web requests while applying content policy.

explanations.task-1: Routers forward packets between networks.
explanations.task-2: Load balancers distribute sessions among servers.
explanations.task-3: An IPS can block malicious traffic inline.
explanations.task-4: NAS provides file-level network storage.
explanations.task-5: A proxy intermediates client web requests.

missions.title: Map the Modern Cloud Roads
missions.objective: N10-009 1.3 and 1.8 — Cloud and modern networking concepts
missions.briefing: Categorize each new service by its primary architecture.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Employees use a complete browser-based collaboration suite.
The network team deploys virtual routers as software on shared compute hosts.
Branches select application-aware paths across multiple WAN links.
A content service processes sensor data near the collection site.

explanations.task-1: SaaS delivers the complete application.
explanations.task-2: NFV runs network functions as software appliances.
explanations.task-3: SD-WAN selects paths using centralized policy.
explanations.task-4: Edge computing places processing near data sources.

missions.title: Open the Approved Service Gates
missions.objective: N10-009 1.4 — Ports, protocols, services, and traffic types
missions.briefing: Configure the service, transport, port, and protected alternative for approved traffic flows.
instructions: Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Secure shell
tasks.prompt: Administrators need encrypted command-line management.

tasks.label: Name service
tasks.prompt: Clients need standard DNS queries.

tasks.label: Web portal
tasks.prompt: Users need encrypted browser access.

explanations.task-1: SSH uses TCP 22 and provides encryption.
explanations.task-2: Ordinary DNS queries commonly use UDP 53 without inherent encryption.
explanations.task-3: HTTPS uses TCP 443 with TLS protection.

missions.title: Identify the Cable Forge
missions.objective: N10-009 1.5 — Cabling, connectors, interfaces, and transceivers
missions.briefing: Identify four interfaces on an original product-neutral termination panel.
instructions: Select the best label for every callout.
Each correct callout earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Identify the twisted-pair Ethernet jack.
Identify the duplex fiber connector.
Identify the coaxial connector.
Identify the modular transceiver cage.

explanations.task-1: The eight-position modular jack is RJ45.
explanations.task-2: The paired compact optical ports represent LC fiber.
explanations.task-3: The threaded round interface is an F-type connector.
explanations.task-4: The rectangular removable-module bay is an SFP-family cage.

visual.alt: Original termination-panel diagram showing an RJ45 jack, duplex LC fiber interface, threaded F-type coaxial connector, and SFP-family transceiver cage.
visual.caption: Hydra connection panel; shapes are simplified and vendor-neutral.

missions.title: Address the Frontier Topology
missions.objective: N10-009 1.6–1.7 — Network topologies, architectures, and addressing
missions.briefing: Assign the correct address scope, prefix, gateway behavior, and segment role.
instructions: Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: User VLAN
tasks.prompt: 10.42.10.0/24 is an internal client subnet routed through 10.42.10.1.

tasks.label: IPv6 LAN
tasks.prompt: 2001:db8:42:20::/64 uses router advertisements for global addressing.

tasks.label: Isolated host
tasks.prompt: A disconnected IPv4 workstation self-assigns 169.254.18.7.

explanations.task-1: The 10.0.0.0/8 range is private and the stated /24 uses its local router.
explanations.task-2: The documentation IPv6 prefix models a /64 SLAAC segment.
explanations.task-3: 169.254.0.0/16 is IPv4 link-local fallback and is not normally routed.

missions.title: Program the Border Routes
missions.briefing: Complete the forwarding decision for three destination networks.
instructions: Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Default
tasks.prompt: Unknown destinations should leave through 192.0.2.1.

tasks.label: Voice
tasks.prompt: 10.60.20.0/24 is directly connected.

tasks.label: Remote lab
tasks.prompt: 10.70.0.0/16 is reached through 198.51.100.9 by a static route.

explanations.task-1: A /0 static route supplies the fallback gateway.
explanations.task-2: A connected subnet needs no next-hop router.
explanations.task-3: The remote /16 uses the stated static next hop.

missions.title: Stabilize the Switch Fabric
missions.briefing: Categorize each switch-port observation by the feature or fault it represents.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A user port carries one untagged workstation VLAN.
An uplink carries tagged traffic for several VLANs.
Two physical uplinks operate as one logical bundle.
A redundant port is intentionally blocking to prevent a loop.
Frames enter one untagged VLAN but leave the trunk with an unexpected native VLAN.

explanations.task-1: An access port carries one endpoint VLAN.
explanations.task-2: A trunk transports multiple tagged VLANs.
explanations.task-3: Link aggregation combines interfaces.
explanations.task-4: STP blocks a redundant path to prevent loops.
explanations.task-5: A native VLAN mismatch can misplace untagged traffic.

missions.title: Coordinate the Wireless Airspace
missions.briefing: Configure band, channel plan, channel width, and security for three coverage zones.
instructions: Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Warehouse
tasks.prompt: Longer reach for scanners; many neighboring 2.4 GHz networks; modest throughput.

tasks.label: Office
tasks.prompt: Modern clients; high density; several nearby APs.

tasks.label: Studio
tasks.prompt: Wi-Fi 6E clients; short range; maximum clean spectrum.

explanations.task-1: A narrow nonoverlapping 2.4 GHz plan favors reach and coexistence.
explanations.task-2: Coordinated 5 GHz channels balance density and throughput.
explanations.task-3: 6 GHz provides clean spectrum for compatible short-range clients.

missions.title: Survey the Network Closet
missions.briefing: Identify four components in an original network-closet diagram.
instructions: Select the best label for every callout.
Each correct callout earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Identify the copper termination panel.
Identify the Ethernet switch.
Identify the horizontal cable manager.
Identify the rack-mounted UPS.

explanations.task-1: The upper row of passive jacks is the patch panel.
explanations.task-2: The active port row with status indicators is the switch.
explanations.task-3: The covered channel organizes patch cords.
explanations.task-4: The heavy lower unit is the UPS.

visual.alt: Original rack diagram with a top copper patch panel, Ethernet switch, horizontal cable manager, and lower uninterruptible power supply.
visual.caption: Simplified Hydra network closet layout.

missions.title: Deploy the New Branch
missions.briefing: Order the controlled deployment of a new branch network.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Validate requirements, site survey findings, diagrams, and rollback plan.
Install approved cabling, rack equipment, power, and environmental controls.
Configure VLANs, trunks, routing, and management access.
Deploy the coordinated wireless configuration.
Test physical links, segmentation, routes, roaming, security, and documentation.

explanations.task-1: Requirements and rollback planning precede changes.
explanations.task-2: Physical infrastructure is installed before logical service.
explanations.task-3: Switching and routing establish the wired foundation.
explanations.task-4: Wireless follows the approved wired design.

missions.title: File the Network Chronicles
missions.briefing: Categorize each artifact by its proper documentation type.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A drawing shows subnets, VLANs, and routed relationships.
A drawing shows rack units, patch panels, and cable paths.
A record stores device serial numbers, owners, and warranties.
A planned switch upgrade includes risk, approval, and rollback.

explanations.task-1: Logical diagrams represent network relationships.
explanations.task-2: Physical diagrams show location and cabling.
explanations.task-3: Asset records track lifecycle data.
explanations.task-4: Change requests govern planned modifications.

missions.title: Read the Monitoring Beacons
missions.briefing: Match each monitoring question to the best telemetry source.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Which interfaces are reporting counters and link state over time?
Which conversations consume the most routed bandwidth?
What exact protocol fields appear in several suspicious packets?
Which devices reported authentication failures to the central collector?
Does the public service respond from an external probe?

explanations.task-1: SNMP supplies device and interface metrics.
explanations.task-2: Flow telemetry summarizes communicating endpoints and volumes.
explanations.task-3: Packet capture exposes protocol fields.
explanations.task-4: Syslog centralizes device event messages.

missions.title: Restore the Flooded Data Hall
missions.briefing: Order the network recovery after the primary site becomes unavailable.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Declare the incident, assess scope, and notify the recovery team.
Activate the approved alternate site and critical connectivity.
Restore required configurations and services from verified copies.
Validate routes, security controls, monitoring, and business applications.
Plan and approve the controlled return to the primary site.

explanations.task-1: Declaration and scope activate the plan.
explanations.task-2: The alternate site supplies recovery capacity.
explanations.task-3: Verified configurations restore network function.
explanations.task-4: Technical and business validation precede use.
explanations.task-5: Failback is a separate controlled change.

missions.title: Assign the Infrastructure Services
missions.objective: N10-009 3.4 — IPv4 and IPv6 network services
missions.briefing: Match each operational symptom to the infrastructure service that should be investigated first.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Clients receive no leases after connecting to a VLAN.
Hostnames fail while direct IP connections succeed.
Logs from different devices show inconsistent timestamps.
IPv6 clients do not form global addresses from router advertisements.
Administrators cannot identify which addresses are allocated or reserved.

explanations.task-1: DHCP distributes IPv4 leases.
explanations.task-2: DNS resolves names to addresses.
explanations.task-3: NTP synchronizes time.
explanations.task-4: Router advertisements support SLAAC.
explanations.task-5: IPAM tracks address usage and reservations.

missions.title: Govern the Management Plane
missions.objective: N10-009 3.5 — Network access and management methods
missions.briefing: Choose the management channel, authentication, source restriction, and logging for each device class.
instructions: Each correct field earns partial credit.

tasks.label: Core switches
tasks.prompt: In-band encrypted CLI from the administration subnet; centralized identity and logs.

tasks.label: Remote router
tasks.prompt: Encrypted management through the approved VPN; centralized identity and logs.

tasks.label: Recovery console
tasks.prompt: Out-of-band serial access from the locked network operations room; local emergency account and session logging.

explanations.task-1: Core switches use restricted encrypted SSH with centralized accountability.
explanations.task-2: The remote router is managed only through the approved encrypted path.
explanations.task-3: Out-of-band console access supports recovery under physical control.

missions.title: Classify the Security Boundaries
missions.briefing: Classify each safeguard by its primary security purpose.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Separate guest devices from internal servers with VLANs and policy.
Require a second factor for network administrators.
Encrypt management traffic between the console and device.
Allow a service account only the permissions required for monitoring.

explanations.task-1: Segmentation limits communication paths.
explanations.task-2: MFA requires another authentication factor.
explanations.task-3: Encryption protects traffic confidentiality.
explanations.task-4: Least privilege limits permissions.

missions.title: Identify the Attack Pattern
missions.briefing: Review each evidence cluster and identify the network attack it represents.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A host sends forged ARP replies and becomes the gateway MAC for nearby clients.
An unauthorized AP advertises the corporate SSID from a conference room.
A switch receives double-tagged frames intended to reach another VLAN.
Resolvers return an attacker-controlled address for a legitimate name.
A public service receives traffic volumes far beyond its capacity.

explanations.task-1: Forged ARP mappings enable local interception.
explanations.task-2: An unauthorized corporate-looking AP is rogue.
explanations.task-3: Double tagging is associated with VLAN hopping.
explanations.task-4: False resolver data indicates DNS poisoning.
explanations.task-5: Resource exhaustion from excessive traffic is denial of service.

missions.title: Layer the Citadel Defenses
missions.objective: N10-009 4.3 — Network security features and defense techniques
missions.briefing: Match each exposure to the defense that most directly reduces it.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Unknown endpoints connect to wall jacks without validation.
A user subnet can directly reach sensitive database interfaces.
Unapproved inbound management traffic reaches routers.
Known exploit traffic crosses an internet edge.
Clients are directed to known malicious domains.

explanations.task-1: NAC validates endpoints before access.
explanations.task-2: Segmentation restricts east-west paths.
explanations.task-3: ACLs filter traffic by defined criteria.
explanations.task-4: IPS can block recognized exploit patterns.
explanations.task-5: Protective DNS blocks resolution of malicious destinations.

missions.title: Follow the Troubleshooting Doctrine
missions.briefing: Order the structured troubleshooting lifecycle.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Identify the problem and gather information.
Establish a theory of probable cause.
Test the theory and determine the cause.
Create a plan of action and identify potential effects.
Implement the solution or escalate as necessary.
Verify full functionality, add preventive measures, and document findings.

explanations.task-1: Evidence gathering defines the problem.
explanations.task-2: A theory focuses testing.
explanations.task-3: Testing confirms or rejects the theory.
explanations.task-4: Planning considers impact before change.
explanations.task-6: Verification and documentation close the incident.

missions.title: Diagnose the Damaged Links
missions.briefing: Classify each tester or interface result.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: A time-domain test shows a conductor ending well before the far connector.
Two conductors contact each other inside the cable.
Continuity exists, but wire pairs are incorrectly combined across pins.
An optical receive level is below the supported power budget.
A switch port and installed fiber module support different wavelengths.

explanations.task-1: An early termination indicates an open.
explanations.task-2: Contact between conductors creates a short.
explanations.task-3: Incorrect pair composition is a split pair.
explanations.task-4: Low optical power indicates excessive loss.
explanations.task-5: Different supported wavelengths prevent the link.

missions.title: Repair the Failing Network Services
missions.objective: N10-009 5.3 — Network services and switching issues
missions.briefing: Categorize each symptom set by its primary fault domain.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Clients in one VLAN receive addresses from the wrong scope.
Names fail but services work by IP address.
One access VLAN cannot cross a trunk while others can.
Switch ports repeatedly transition because of a Layer 2 loop.
Hosts reach local peers but not remote networks after a router change.

explanations.task-1: Wrong-scope leases indicate DHCP configuration.
explanations.task-2: Name-only failure points to DNS.
explanations.task-3: One missing VLAN points to trunk allowance.
explanations.task-4: Port transitions and loops implicate STP.
explanations.task-5: Remote-only failure after router change points to the gateway.

missions.title: Resolve the Performance Storm
missions.objective: N10-009 5.4 — Network performance and wireless issues
missions.briefing: Classify each performance evidence set.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Uplink utilization remains near capacity during business hours and queues grow.
Nearby APs use overlapping channels and retransmission rates rise.
Round-trip time increases substantially while packet delivery remains reliable.
Interface counters show late collisions and negotiation differs at each end.
Wireless signal strength is high but many frames require retransmission near a microwave oven.

explanations.task-1: Sustained saturation and queues indicate congestion.
explanations.task-2: Overlapping channels cause contention and retries.
explanations.task-3: High round-trip time is latency.
explanations.task-4: Late collisions with negotiation differences indicate duplex mismatch.
explanations.task-5: Retries near an RF source indicate interference.

missions.title: Choose the Diagnostic Instruments
missions.objective: N10-009 5.5 — Network troubleshooting tools and protocols
missions.briefing: Match each investigation goal to the best first tool.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Inspect exact protocol fields in a failed exchange.
Locate a break along a copper cable run.
Measure nearby wireless channels and signal levels.
Identify the routed hop where latency begins.
Query a specific DNS record type.
Discover listening TCP ports on an approved test host.

explanations.task-1: Packet capture reveals protocol fields.
explanations.task-2: A cable tester locates physical faults.
explanations.task-3: A Wi-Fi analyzer surveys channels and signal.
explanations.task-4: Traceroute reveals the hop path.
explanations.task-6: A port scanner tests listening services when authorized.

missions.title: Recover the Divided Kingdom
missions.briefing: Order recovery of a multi-site outage with several independent faults.
instructions: Each correct task earns one point.

tasks.prompt: Establish scope using user reports, monitoring, diagrams, and recent changes.
Restore the failed physical uplink after confirming the cable fault.
Correct the switch trunk VLAN mismatch revealed after link restoration.
Repair the DHCP relay configuration affecting the recovered branch VLAN.
Adjust the congested wireless channel plan using survey evidence.
Verify wired, routed, service, and wireless operation; document each root cause.

explanations.task-1: Scope and evidence separate multiple faults.
explanations.task-2: The physical path must function before higher-layer testing.
explanations.task-3: Correct trunk transport restores the VLAN path.
explanations.task-4: DHCP relay depends on the restored routed VLAN.
explanations.task-5: Wireless optimization follows core service recovery.
